questions.question: What is the support of a Rayleigh distribution?
options: All integers
Only $0$ and $1$
All values in a fixed finite interval
Nonnegative values

questions.question: What condition is required for the Rayleigh parameter $\sigma$?
options: $\sigma>0$
$\sigma=0$
$\sigma<0$
$\sigma$ must equal $1/2$

questions.question: What kind of quantity does the Rayleigh distribution often describe?
options: The number of successes in fixed trials
The exact value of a Bernoulli outcome
The order of a finite sample
The magnitude of a two-dimensional random vector

questions.question: What is the general shape behavior of a Rayleigh density?
options: It is constant on its support
It has a jump from zero to one
It is positive only at one point.
Starts at zero, peaks, then decays.

questions.question: What normal-vector construction produces a Rayleigh distribution?
options: The sum of two Bernoulli indicators
The number of events in a fixed time interval.
The first trial on which success occurs
Magnitude of two independent centered normals, equal var.

questions.question: Which example can be modeled by a Rayleigh distribution?
options: The number of heads in ten tosses
The number of aces in a hand
A fixed value equal to five
Wind speed magnitude

questions.question: Which value is impossible for a Rayleigh random variable?
If a distance error comes from two independent normal coordinate errors, which distribution may describe its magnitude?
options: Rayleigh
Bernoulli
Hypergeometric
Poisson

questions.question: For a Rayleigh density, what is $f_X(0)$ from the displayed formula?
options: $1/\sigma$
$1/\sigma^2$

questions.question: Which model is more natural for signal envelope amplitudes in some noise models?
options: Discrete uniform distribution
Rayleigh distribution
Geometric distribution
Degenerate distribution at zero

questions.question: Why is the Rayleigh distribution not appropriate for negative observations?
options: Its density is constant on all real numbers
It has no density
It only models integers
Its support is restricted to nonnegative values

questions.question: Why does a Rayleigh distribution appear from two normal components?
options: Adding two normal variables always creates a count
Euclidean magnitude turns two coordinate errors into a distance.
Taking a logarithm of a normal variable creates a distance.
Sampling without replacement creates a magnitude

questions.question: What role does $\sigma$ play in the Rayleigh density?
options: It is a positive scale parameter
It is a probability of success
It is the number of trials
It is the fixed value of a degenerate distribution

questions.question: If $\sigma=2$, which expression is the Rayleigh density for $x\ge0$?
Which observed variable is closest to the Rayleigh interpretation?
options: Distance from a target after two coordinate errors.
The number of defective items in a sample.
The number of arrivals in ten minutes
The outcome of one coin toss

questions.question: If a Rayleigh model is proposed for signed temperature error, what is a concern?
options: Signed errors can be negative; Rayleigh is nonnegative.
Rayleigh variables cannot describe magnitudes.
Rayleigh variables must be integers
Rayleigh variables have variance zero

questions.question: Why can a Rayleigh density start at zero but still assign positive probability to intervals away from zero?
options: The density is a probability mass at zero
All probability must be placed at the peak
Intervals away from zero are outside the support
Density at a point is not the same as interval probability

questions.question: Why is a Rayleigh variable not the same object as a folded normal variable?
options: Rayleigh variables can take negative values, while folded normal variables cannot.
Folded normal variables require two independent normal coordinates.
Both distributions are identical whenever the normal mean is zero.
Rayleigh is a two-coordinate radius; folded normal is one-coordinate absolute value.

questions.question: If $X$ is Rayleigh, what is $P(X<0)$?
options: $\sigma$

questions.question: A Rayleigh density is written with $\sigma=-3$. What is wrong?
options: The parameter must satisfy $\sigma>0$
The support should be all integers
The variable $x$ must be allowed to be negative
The value $x=0$ must be excluded
